lesson.title: Computers and Staying Safe
lesson.summary: Inputs and outputs, using devices well, electricity safety, private information and being kind online.
learning_objectives: Say what inputs and outputs are
Keep private things private and be kind online

standards.text: Recognise common uses of information technology; use technology safely and respectfully, keeping personal information private
Select and operate appropriate software and hardware to perform a variety of tasks
Explain why we keep information private, such as passwords
Compare how people live and work before and after the adoption of computing technologies

success_criteria: I can name an input and an output
I know what to do if something online worries me
I know how to stay safe with plugs
lesson.real_life: Using the family tablet, charging a phone and chatting with relatives online.

sub_lessons.title: Inside a computer: in and out

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we use computers safely?
blocks.say: Today we learn how computers work and how to stay safe.

blocks.say: A padlock keeps things safe. A password does the same job for us.

blocks.text: Stop 1: How we talk to a computer

blocks.markdown:
An **input** is how we tell a computer something.

An **output** is how the computer tells us something.
blocks.say: A computer is a machine that follows instructions. But how do we tell it what to do? We use things called inputs. A keyboard is an input. A mouse is an input. A touch screen is an input too. We put information in. The computer thinks, and then it gives us an answer. That answer is called an output.

scenes.caption: Input: a keyboard.
scenes.say: First, an input. We press a key on the keyboard.

scenes.caption: The computer works it out.
scenes.say: The computer receives it and works on it. This is the thinking part.

scenes.caption: Output: a screen and a speaker.
scenes.say: Then comes the output. The screen shows the answer, and the speaker plays a sound.

question.explanation: We use a keyboard to put information in.

blocks.markdown:
A **tablet**, a **laptop** and a phone are all computers.

Even a washing machine has a tiny computer inside.
blocks.say: Computers come in many shapes. A tablet is a computer. A phone is a computer. A laptop is a computer. Even a washing machine and a car have tiny computers inside. They all take inputs, think, and give outputs.

blocks.alt: A phone, a laptop, a desktop and a car all use computers.
blocks.caption: A phone, a laptop, a desktop and a car all use computers.

question.prompt: A screen is an output because it shows us information.
question.hint: Does it show or tell us?
question.explanation: A screen shows us things, so it is an output.

blocks.title: Zainab stays safe
blocks.transcript: Zainab uses the family tablet. A touch screen is input and output. The keyboard is an input. The speaker is an output. After twenty minutes, Zainab takes a break. Her eyes need a rest. Her password is a secret key. Only Mum knows it. A stranger in a game asks where she lives. She does not answer. She tells Mum straight away. Telling is always right. Then she sends Nani a kind message with Mum's help. Plugs are for grown-ups. Zainab never touches sockets.
blocks.caption: Zainab uses the tablet safely and kindly.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Using devices well and being safe with electricity

blocks.alt: A white wall socket on a blue wall
blocks.caption: A wall socket. Never touch it. Ask a grown-up.
blocks.credit: Photo by Gleb Paniotov on Unsplash
blocks.say: This is a wall socket. Never touch it. Ask a grown-up.

blocks.markdown:
Use devices well: take **breaks**.

Be safe with **electricity**: never touch sockets and ask a grown-up.
blocks.say: Devices are fun, but we should use them well. Take breaks, sit up straight and keep the screen at a good distance. Remember to keep your eyes healthy. And electricity is powerful. Never put fingers or things into plug sockets. Never touch plugs with wet hands. Always ask a grown-up to help with plugs and cables.

sub_lessons.title: Private information and being kind online

blocks.markdown: **Private** information is just for you and your family. A **password** is a secret key.
blocks.say: Some information is private. Private means only for you and your family. Your full name, your address, your school, and your passwords are all private. We never share them online. A password is like a secret key. If you share it, someone else might get in. Only share a password with your parent.

blocks.alt: A password is like a secret key. Keep it private.
blocks.caption: A password is like a secret key. Keep it private.

question.prompt: Which is private information we should NOT share online?

blocks.markdown: Be **kind** online. If something worries you, **tell a grown-up**.
blocks.say: Being kind online is just like being kind in real life. We say please and thank you. We write friendly messages. If someone is unkind, tell a grown-up straight away. Do the same if you feel worried. You will not be in trouble.

blocks.caption: Kind messages make people smile.
blocks.say: Kind messages make people smile, online and in real life.
